posts.body_html: meizzwang when did those traps open? They look pretty fresh aka late summer flush. My clone has a red lip / throat area on the spring traps (as does yours I think) but it is a specimen-sized clump with many traps in good condition from the spring. It's not throwing too many fall traps (yet) but division that is a single GP is opening robust colorful fall traps now. Wonder if light penetration is a trigger for fall traps in oreo too?

posts.body_html:
Looking great meizzwang ! Seems like some clones will consistently produce a robust set of fall traps while others won't. My purple clone seems to be a consistent late pitcherer. My big clump of this plant only produced fall traps on the south side of the pot (it's pretty dense with spring traps and phyllodia), which makes me think that light could be an important factor to get them to initiate, just like in S. leucophylla.
A late season trap on my clone:
IMG_1685 by Calen Hall, on Flickr
